subject: Private cert flow for on-prem runtime — CSR puller & split-horizon mapping

Subject: On-prem certs & DNS for private endpoint — compliance ask

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the earlier call. We need a short written plan for how Redwood will handle TLS + DNS for our on-prem deployment (FinPay prod edge). Our compliance team requires:
- A signed cert workflow that works in an air-gapped datacenter (we use an internal offline CA).
- Split-horizon DNS approach so public redirection isn’t leaked.
- Clear owner of TLS termination (customer gateway vs Redwood runtime).

Attached is our CSR (finpay_onprem_csr.pem) and our checklist; please confirm whether the CSR puller approach you mentioned in the call is acceptable, and outline the operational steps and who does what.

Goal: Sign-off by FinPay security by EOD Friday so the procurement loop can finish next week.

Thanks,
Paul Simmons\Security & Compliance\FinPay
From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem certs & DNS for private endpoint — compliance ask

Paul — thanks for the CSR and checklist. Looping in Jonas and Karthik for the deep ops details and Marissa for the contract ramifications. Quick summary of the proposal we discussed on the call (high level):

1) Certificate provisioning model (recommended): "CSR puller" agent that runs inside FinPay VPC/on-prem environment. Behavior:
   - Redwood generates a CSR template or accepts customer CSR (like the attached).
   - The agent (customer-run) establishes an outbound-only TLS connection to Redwood control plane using pre-shared bootstrap token and requests the CSR be signed.
   - The CSR is forwarded to FinPay's offline CA operator out-of-band (manual or automated connector), signed, and the signed cert is returned to the agent which writes it into local keystore.

   Rationale: no inbound holes required; supports air-gapped CA workflows because signing can be manual and then returned to the agent.

2) TLS termination options (choose one):
   A) Customer terminates TLS at their local ingress (recommended for strict compliance). Redwood traffic to runtime is plaintext on internal LAN or mTLS if customer wants mutual auth.
   B) Redwood terminates TLS at a private endpoint inside customer network (requires Redwood runtime component inside VPC and private key escrow considerations).

3) DNS split-horizon:
   - Public DNS points at public endpoints (if any).
   - Private FQDN (prod-internal.finpay.local or *.finpay.internal) is configured in customer DNS or split-horizon view and points to the internal ingress.
   - TTLs short for rapid failover.

4) OCSP/CRL and rotation: offline CA implies CRLs published externally are not reliable; recommend short cert lifetimes (30-90 days) and documented manual rotation process with an emergency cert-escrow key held by FinPay.

Next steps: Jonas — can you sketch the operational runbook and agent behavior? Karthik — any objections on the mapping policy and key lifecycle? Marissa — pricing/contract flags if we need on-prem support agents and HAC backups.

Thanks, Mina\nMina Haddad\Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments\Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: On-prem certs & DNS for private endpoint — compliance ask

FWIW, I drafted the runbook and included it on Drive (link above). Key ops specifics and deviations from a standard ACME flow:

- Agent lifecycle: bootstrap token created by FinPay SRE, passed to agent installer. Agent only opens outbound port 443 to Redwood control-plane IPs; all CSR traffic is authenticated with the bootstrap token + agent TLS identity.
- CSR handling modes:
  1) Customer-supplied CSR (you provided one) — agent uploads CSR to a signed queue; CA operator fetches, signs offline, places signed cert in a secure return queue. Agent pulls it and installs.
  2) Redwood-generated CSR — agent generates keypair locally and submits CSR; Redwood can stage CSR for CA operator review but does not hold private key at any point.
- Key storage: recommended hardware-backed keystore on gateway (TPM/HSM) for private key protection. If not possible, use encrypted disk with restricted permissions and an operator-run key-rotation script.
- SNI mapping and routing:    
  - Use SNI on the ingress to map to backend tenant. For non-SNI clients, add an explicit IP-based mapping as fallback.
- OCSP: since FinPay CA is offline, treat OCSP stapling as N/A. Use short cert TTL and monitor expiry with Prometheus alerting pushed to FinPay pager.

Open question for FinPay: do you want Redwood to operate a standby private endpoint in case of gateway failure (we can provide a redundant runtime in a colocation if you permit cross-network peering)? This will require explicit contract language for cross-network routing.

Jonas\Infra/SRE\Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side:
- We prefer mode (1): customer-supplied CSR and offline signing — that meets our policy.
- We will not permit private key export from the gateway (TPM recommended).
- We cannot allow Redwood-controlled standby endpoints that cross our network boundary. So no cross-peering backups.

Action items for Redwood:
1) Provide a minimal agent package (binary + install flags) and the exact bootstrap token creation steps.
2) Produce a short runbook for our CA operator: how to fetch pending CSRs and where to upload signed certs.
3) Confirm monitoring hooks so our team gets a cert-expiry alert 14 days before expiry.

Can you send those by tomorrow morning? If so we can greenlight the procurement doc and sign the SLA.

Paul

- No cross-network standby endpoints will be provisioned.
